candidates.exact_span:
* If the flow from the outfall(s) being tested ceases during the collection of effluent
      samples, the requirements for the minimum number of effluent samples and the minimum
      number of effluent portions are waived during that sampling period. However, the
      permittee must collect an effluent composite sample volume during the period of
      discharge that is sufficient to complete the required toxicity tests with daily renewal of
      effluent, and must meet the holding time between collection and first use of the sample.
      When possible, the effluent samples used for the toxicity tests shall be collected on
      separate days. The effluent composite sample collection duration and the static renewal
      protocol associated with the abbreviated sample collection must be documented in the
      full report required in Item 3 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ambiguity over what counts as flow cessation, how much sampling is waived versus still required, and what volume is 'sufficient' changes which monitoring obligations apply during intermittent discharge (B) and whether a period is documented no-discharge, conditionally excused from minimum sampling, or lacking adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span:
**Test failure may not be construed or reported as invalid due to a coefficient of
      variation value of greater than 40%, or a PMSD value greater than the higher value on the
      range provided.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This carve-out conflicts with the table CV criterion; interpreting when a high CV or PMSD still yields a valid result versus an invalid one changes whether toxicity measurements are used in numeric limit exceedance evaluation (A) and how anomalous test statistics are categorized in missing-evidence semantics (C).

candidates.locator: Page 14, Section part_i, subsection a. Statistical Interpretation
candidates.exact_span:
a. Statistical Interpretation
      The statistical analyses used to determine if there is a significant difference between the
      control and the critical dilution shall be in accordance with the methods for determining
      the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) as described in the appropriate method
      manual listed in Part II or the most recent update thereof.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Choice among Part II method manuals or 'the most recent update thereof' changes the NOEC/significance determination, which can change whether a reported toxicity measurement is treated as exceeding the applicable numeric limit.

candidates.locator: Page 14, Section part_i, subsection b. Dilution Water, item 1)i.
candidates.exact_span:
b. Dilution Water

          1) Dilution water used in the toxicity tests will be receiving water collected as close
             to the point of discharge as possible but unaffected by the discharge. The
             permittee shall substitute synthetic dilution water of similar pH, hardness, and
             alkalinity to the closest downstream perennial water for;
                  i. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges to receiving water
                     classified as intermittent streams; and
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a discharge is classified as an intermittent stream and whether synthetic dilution water substitution was required changes applicable toxicity monitoring protocol obligations (B), whether reported results used the correct test matrix for limit comparison (A), and whether absent or alternate dilution-water documentation reflects conditional non-requirement or inadequate evidence (C).
